members.title: 触乐本周行业大事：从业者怎么看？光子公布怪谈RPG新作，《影之刃：零》发布最终预告，Steam新品节AI游戏占比超三成

news.body:
还有《蓝色星原：旅谣》定档、《使命召唤：现代战争4》《影之刃：零》领跑Steam销量榜，以及几个行业新动向。
“每周行业大事”是触乐在每周六的固定栏目，触乐编辑会当本周发生的行业事件中选出有价值的新闻，并告诉大家或许哪些事更值得关注。在这个过程中，我们希望这档栏目能够更加面向从业者，并了解哪些事情是大家切实关心的。
因此，在本周的行业大事里，我们邀请了几位从业者来和我们一起整理新闻。在编辑挑出的新闻中，他们会自由地针对自己感兴趣的部分留下看法。藉由这个机会，我们也希望看看从业者更关心哪些事件，以及会从什么角度来看待它们。
如果您喜欢这样的形式，或者有更好的建议，也欢迎留言告诉我们！
10月21日，腾讯光子工作室群旗下H.STUDIO（宇宙小狗工作室/COSMICPUP STUDIO）正式公布开放世界RPG《人间异想计划》，同步放出22分钟的实机PV。产品定位为"轻怪谈都市异想开放世界RPG"。据悉，开发团队位于杭州滨江，负责人叶谦（羊头）为前网易杭州F工作室负责人、在网易任职16年（项目包括《大话西游外传》《黑潮之上》《阴阳师：妖怪小班》《光明大陆》《终结者2》等），2021年离职加入腾讯。
策划-斯凯：新怪谈确实是近两年二次元方面在挖掘的新题材，像归龙潮、1999、异环、白银之城都在走这个路子，但是这需要真的有人懂怎么把新怪谈的那个味儿做得能让大众认可。国内在这方面的积累很少，加上新怪谈在国内属于小众群体，再加上大投入，最终势必要在大众审美和小众题材之间来回摇摆，挺有挑战性的。
策划-皮卡皮：怪谈这个方向其实还没有真正出现“标杆”性质的作品，而这个题材本身在小说或者影视作品里都有比较强的吸引力，所以我觉得其实还是有机会的。目前从PV和玩家的主要讨论来看，整体还是在具体玩法、战斗上没有足够的呈现，这部分其实才是让玩家留下来的重点，希望团队可以在之后带来一些新的突破吧。
杭州千乎网络自研手游《辉烬》iOS端总收入不足200万元，不到研发成本零头；到今年6月iOS月下载量跌至不足五千，分账后月收入约6000美元。6月底百人项目组全员解散，9月30日公司正式进入注销公告程序（45日内债权人申报）。
木子岚工作室是《辉烬》美术外包之一，项目存续期间多次公开表示未收到外包款，公司解散后彻底无门，直到10月16日仍未拿到钱。在法律追讨希望渺茫后，他们用手里的美术资源把《辉烬》重做成买断制PC单机动作游戏《辉烬：南星》。
某位手持大水的策划 ：直截了当地说，其实就是公司破产之后，被外包公司搜打撤了……只是从原本的实体资产变成了数字资产。但是或许是因为之前很少有公司愿意把一款已经证明不成功的游戏重新打包制作吧，所以才成了新闻。感觉外包团队在很大程度上确实对产品也抱有感情了。
策划-皮卡皮：我更好奇的是，在这种情况下，游戏作为虚拟资产能值多少钱。
Valve公布10月13日—10月20日Steam销量榜（不含免费游戏）。《使命召唤：现代战争4》预购即登顶全球与国区双榜第一；同时，《影之刃零》预购国区第二、全球第十；上期榜首《AION2》直接跌出榜单。
某位手持大水的策划 ：这一作证明了年货模式依然还是能走通的，尤其是AI能力不断提升的情况下，开发效率想必也有了很大的提升。但需要注意的是，23号晚上，我特地看了下，《影之刃：零》已经变成了国区第一、全球第六！
策划-皮卡皮：作为年货游戏，但每年都能卖得好，某种程度上，它其实也可以叫“长青系列游戏”吧？
10月22日，灵游坊放出《影之刃：零》3分10秒的最终预告，游戏将于10月27日10点预载、10月29日10点正式发售。
同日，根据Alinea Analytics估算，Steam预购数约为50万份；截至2026年10月20日，估算国区愿望单约250万。
策划-皮卡皮：黑神话给人的销量还是太过梦幻，现在再看影之刃的预售情况反而会觉得踏实很多。如果一切顺利，它更有可能成为一个国产3A团队能够努力追上的目标。
某位手持大水的策划 ：这条上面说过了，然后我和甄子丹及其武术团队在月底有一场线上交流会……
据SteamDB统计，10月Steam新品节7145款参展游戏中，约2596款（36.4%）在开发中披露使用了生成式AI，较6月的19%四个月上涨16个百分点。
《花冠战略》制作人-潇潇：AI的趋势无法避免，未来当这个比例进一步上升之后，AI内容披露的选项可以能会失去意义，用户最终只会以品质来判断。
策划-斯凯：未来steam可能也会变成小游戏平台那样每天巨量上架的游戏在里面搏杀抢流量，如果steam坚持不在导量上去盈利的话，那就是看谁经营社群的能力强了，第三方发行公司可能会来承接这部分的业务。
苹果全球App Store负责人卡森·奥利弗（Carson Oliver）接受采访表示，今年登陆App Store的精品付费游戏数量超过去年，越来越多原本面向PC与主机的作品正进入iPhone/iPad生态。他特别提到《小丑牌》《星露谷物语》《杀戮尖塔》《BloonsTD6》，称治愈类、经营模拟、Roguelike在移动端表现突出。
策划-斯凯：对于所有小体量独游而言，支持双端是收入最大化的必然选择。
10月19日，国家网信办发布公告，为进一步强化未成年人网络保护，压实网络平台主体责任，国家网信办近日发布公告，启动未成年人用户数量巨大和对未成年人群体具有显著影响的网络平台服务提供者认定工作。
根据4月1日起施行的《未成年人用户数量巨大和对未成年人群体具有显著影响的网络平台服务提供者认定办法》，被认定为未成年人用户数量巨大的网络平台服务提供者的，应当符合以下情形之一：该网络平台提供的产品或者服务专门以未成年人为服务对象，注册用户在1000万以上或者月活跃用户在100万以上；该网络平台提供的产品或者服务的对象不局限于未成年人的，未成年人注册用户数量在1000万以上或者月活跃未成年人用户在100万以上。
《花冠战略》制作人-潇潇：互联网保护未成年人的行动已经采取了很多年，但未成年人无论是沉迷小网络社交也好，现在的AI陪伴也罢，核心还是很多情感陪伴类需求无法在现实生活中满足。如果真实的家人能够提供优质的陪伴，那这些都不会是问题；如何构建一个父母、家庭能够为未成年人带来更好幸福感的社会，才是解决这一类问题的核心。
10月21日，作为中国音像与数字出版协会主管的中国游戏产业研究专家委员会的战略合作伙伴，伽马数据发布了《2026年7—9月中国游戏产业季度报告》。
数据显示，
2026年7—9月，中国游戏市场实际销售收入为925.22亿元，环比增长1.36%，同比增长5.11%。暑期消费窗口释放市场活力。
2026年7—9月，中国客户端游戏市场实际销售收入为205.47亿元，环比增长1.16%，同比增长1.26%。市场增长主要受头部产品运营活动与新品供给共同驱动。
2026年7—9月，中国移动游戏市场实际销售收入为678.20亿元，环比增长0.34%，同比增长5.33%。市场收入保持增长，主要受到长线产品运营活动与新品收入贡献的共同影响。
2026年7-9月，中国自主研发游戏海外市场实际销售收入达57.72亿美元，环比下降4.46%，同比增长15.58%。环比下滑主要受成熟产品影响。
策划-斯凯：游戏大部分赛道已经是红海了，除了国内pc国内企业还没有大规模参与外，其他赛道都在找新的盈利模式。出海可能还有些盈利空间，靠着手游上的成熟运营模式去吊打海外。PC端游盘子小投入大，国内缺积累，只能是小厂或独立工作室去抢占。现在只能看AI会带来怎样的新方向了。不过哪怕环境再差，能成功的终归是那些用心做自己喜欢游戏的。
10月23日，蛮啾网络官宣《蓝色星原：旅谣》公测定档11月26日。该作自2024年首曝后历经多轮测试，最近一轮“旅迹测试”于9月结束，全球预约量已突破2500万。
策划-皮卡皮：从测试结果来说大概会有点前途多舛的感觉，但他们的美术又很好地弥补了这一点。但我感觉比较担心的，其实是游戏上线之后会不会被定性成下一个《尘白禁区》。做市场推广的时候或许还是要更慎重一些……
最后，我们问了问，几位从业者最关心的新闻是哪些：
《花冠战略》制作人-潇潇：Steam新品节的新闻吧。因为我正在目睹冲击的过程，之前AI影响画师/配音演员，我都是旁观者，现在就是感觉真正被冲击到。
策划-斯凯：AI、PC相关的新闻吧，因为我个人在用ai做demo，平时玩pc游戏比较多。
策划-皮卡皮：我其实对外包那个新闻挺感兴趣的，感觉大的行业新闻都有点司空见惯 ，反而这种非常规的新闻会更容易吸引我。

news.body:
Get This Free Blender Add-On That Makes Hair Meshes Thinner at the Ends
MT Hair Taper gives hairstyles a smoother, more realistic look.
Take a look at MT Hair Taper, a free Blender add-on from 3D Artist MOTOMODEL that tapers the ends of hair-strand meshes for a more natural look.
The add-on preserves the strand's length and shape, narrowing it only in width. It is designed for grid-like hair-strand meshes, where quad faces are arranged vertically and horizontally, and where a horizontal row of vertices can be traced in sequence from the tip to the root.
The tool works well for hair bundles made from flat plane meshes and can also be used on cylindrical meshes that are closed horizontally. It is not suited to meshes with many triangles, radial vertex flow, or irregular divisions where a horizontal row can't be identified. The effect applies only to the part of the mesh where that grid continues from the selected row. Note that the add-on requires Blender 4.0 or later.

news.summary_raw: Tiny Brutalism brings concrete architecture to the cozy city builder genre.

members.title: Check Out This Relaxing Brutalist City Builder Inspired by Tiny Glade

news.body:
Check Out This Relaxing Brutalist City Builder Inspired by Tiny Glade
Tiny Brutalism brings concrete architecture to the cozy city builder genre.
If you are a fan of cozy games, especially titles such as Tiny Glade or Townscraper, check out Tiny Brutalism from Jimjum Studios, which inverts the genre of cozy builders and adds a twist of an unexpected architectural style – brutalism.
In the sandbox, you can create your own dream mega structure using over 20 building blocks, which perfectly fit into procedurally generated buildings, bridges, towers, stairs, and nature. The game features immersive environments with trees, bushes, and vines, and the architecture looks realistic with various concrete textures.
Jimjum Studios
The devs share that they feel brutalism is an underexplored genre, and much more popular than people tend to assume. There's a unique feature to add interiors and in-door decorating, as leading sandbox city builders don't support this, and you can even explore your own creations with the first-person mode and explore what you've built from the eyes of a citizen, also jumping around and performing parkour. The city builder is being developed with Unity, and the developers utilize our own in-house tools.
Jimjum Studios
Tiny Brutalism features a weather system with a day and night cycle, where you control the environment with rain and fog. There are no goals or roght ways to build – the gameplay is relaxing, calm, and atmospheric, and you can just enjoy the process and craft your own brutalist utopia. The game is in development, and the creators promise more exciting features to come.
Jimjum Studios

news.title: BioWare's end is a tragically familiar tale | Opinion
news.summary_raw: After the past five years of seemingly endless closures, cancellations, and restructures, after the tens of thousands of layoffs that the industry has endured like a relentless drumbeat, you'd think that we'd all have grown some pretty thick skin. How much can one more bad news story really hurt?

members.title: BioWare's end is a tragically familiar tale | Opinion

news.body:
BioWare's end is a tragically familiar tale | Opinion
No other studio ever matched BioWare's 15 year run of excellence. But all too many share the story of the last ten years – talented teams undermined by weak, trend-chasing mismanagement
After the past five years of seemingly endless closures, cancellations, and restructures, after the tens of thousands of layoffs that the industry has endured like a relentless drumbeat, you'd think that we'd all have grown some pretty thick skin. How much can one more bad news story really hurt?
A lot, it turns out. Losing BioWare stings.
It's not the sting of surprise, to be clear. The speed with which the newly private-equity-owned Electronic Arts moved to shutter the studio was unexpected, but the outcome was grimly predictable. The foundational logic of a private equity buyout is that some finance types have looked at a business and concluded that they can load it up with debt which it'll pay back by slashing costs. BioWare was never likely to survive that process intact, if at all.
It's not even, if we're being honest, a sting of injustice, per se. The cutting of so many jobs at a studio (among a total of 400 being slashed across EA) alongside the cancellation of the project it was working on will never feel fair or right, especially when the decisions that led to it were so entirely out of the control of the talented people who now find themselves facing unemployment. But in a broader view, if the knife had to fall somewhere (which it did not), you can see why it fell here.
The BioWare being snuffed out this week isn't the BioWare now being lamented so widely. It's still a studio of remarkable, skilled, passionate people, but it's a studio that hasn't had a critical or commercial hit in over a decade – the (genuinely phenomenal) Dragon Age: Inquisition was the last flash of real BioWare magic. It doesn't look good on paper, and paper is all that the people making these decisions look at.
To make things worse, the new Mass Effect game the studio was working on was described as being in "early development", despite its first trailer being shown almost six years ago. "Early development" is a vague term, but for a big AAA game like this it implies that release was still several years, hundreds of millions of dollars, and probably a hardware generation away. An expensive long-term gamble on a franchise whose last outing didn't do well and which doesn't sit neatly into the sport, military shooter, and live service buckets that EA's new owners actually seem interested in – those odds were never going to work out.
What stings isn't even just nostalgia for the incredible studio that BioWare was for such a long time. The studio of Baldur's Gate and Neverwinter Nights, games which more or less resurrected Dungeons & Dragons from cultural limbo, without which pop-culture phenomena like Stranger Things simply wouldn't exist. The studio of Knights of the Old Republic and my personal favourite, Jade Empire. The studio that, even after being bought by legendary mis-manager and destroyer of talented studios Electronic Arts, still released Mass Effect and Dragon Age.
From 1998 to 2014, BioWare had a run that I'm not sure any other development studio has ever equalled. The notion that it's now gone (or worse, that it now exists only as a disembodied piece of IP, a brand-name that will eventually be dusted off and skin-puppeted about by private equity ghouls) is certainly hard to swallow, even if its halcyon days were quite a long time ago.
No, what really stings isn't the loss, or the single decision that ended the studio's existence. It's the nigh-on decade and a half of decisions that led here; the gruesome mismanagement of an iconic, fabulously creative studio. It's the litany of bad choices and trend-chasing and interference.
Most of all, it's the grinding, awful familiarity of it – the knowledge that the song of how BioWare died is one that most of the rest of the industry can hum the tune of by heart, even if the specific lyrics change a little. This happens over and over again, and the people who ought to learn, never learn, because they're never the ones having to brush up their CVs and think about how long their emergency savings will last.
The private equity acquisition of EA was only the final coup de grace to a studio that had already taken body blows from every awful trend the games industry has experienced in the past couple of decades. With the clarity of hindsight – unfair as that might be – you can already start to see the seeds of disaster in the weird attempts to make multiplayer modes a core part of the Mass Effect franchise. It was odd even at the time, but now it looks like a clear indication of how uncomfortably the industry's most celebrated creator of story-driven, single-player experiences would sit within the structure of the eternally trend-chasing EA.
EA decreed that single-player games must be made multiplayer, no matter how ill-fitting that was
That was the era in which plenty of publishing execs convinced themselves that single-player gaming was on the way out, so EA decreed that single-player games must be made multiplayer, no matter how ill-fitting that was or how much of a distraction from the core development effort it became. (Mass Effect arguably got off lightly compared to the Dead Space franchise, at least.)
This was only a prelude to the real disaster, of course; by the time live service became the trend to chase, BioWare had seen the departure of many of its veteran leaders, including co-founders Ray Muzyka and Greg Zeschuk, and with them any hope of an anchor against the buffeting winds of EA's commands. There's a pretty strong argument that BioWare actually died with the failure of its massively expensive live-service flop, Anthem. That disaster really left only a shell stumbling forward with little consistent direction until another game originally intended to be live service before being hastily reworked, Dragon Age: The Veilguard, limped out the door in 2024.
Veilguard will now be BioWare's last game. It's not a good game, but also not entirely as bad as people make out. I finished it, which is actually a somewhat rare accolade these days, and found it to be a fascinating mess that's really an apt summary of everything that had gone wrong for the studio under EA mismanagement. Some parts are beautiful, atmospheric, and superbly written; two minutes later you can be in the midst of slapdash nonsense listening to painful dialogue that clearly never felt the gentle caress of an editor's pen. The seams where the whole thing was stitched together from multiple iterations of very different games, including the mad, awful idea of a live service Dragon Age title, are impossible to miss.
It's a shambling, stitched-together monster of a thing, scarred by bad decisions and traumatised by constant shifts in creative direction, animated by fascinating glimmers of creative talent and still, ultimately, far less than the sum of its mismatched parts. It's a game that could only have been made by a studio being ordered to pursue different goals and visions from week to week to week; no mad auteur could ever dream up such a perfect encapsulation of mismanagement and executive folly.
The gap between the extraordinary focus, polish, and clarity of vision seen in BioWare's best games and the sense of complete inconsistency and uncertainty about itself seen in Veilguard (let alone the almost total lack of character and depth in Anthem five years earlier) tells a clear and tragic story. The creative staff at BioWare didn't suddenly forget how to make good games, or how to write good dialogue, design good combat systems, or build intriguing worlds. The entire framework that's required to actually do that needs stability, consistency, and clear direction that aligns with the creative values of the project – none of which EA ever provided to the studio.
The real tragedy is how ordinary this particular brand of villainy has become in this industry
Is EA the villain that killed BioWare? Ultimately, yes – yet another trophy from a legendary studio to go on its grisly serial killer's wall – but the real tragedy is how ordinary this particular brand of villainy has become in this industry, especially when private equity is there to put a knife in its hand. Giving the goose what it needs to keep laying golden eggs is just beyond the ken of a great many people in decision-making positions. That doesn't mean buying studios and then just leaving them to their own devices (Microsoft seems to have attempted something like that during the Phil Spencer era, with disastrous results of its own). But there must be some middle ground between that and carving off cuts of a fowl while occasionally stopping to complain that you haven't seen a golden egg lately.
I don't have a smart solution or pithy suggestion to close on. The studio that made some of my favourite games ever is gone, and 400 people have lost their jobs. Many of the people who made the worst decisions along the way to this sad ending have probably done very nicely out of the private equity deal that brought the final hammer down, and thus will learn nothing, because nobody ever learns from mistakes that someone else pays the price for. Raise a glass to BioWare, but leave a dram in the bottle, because it won't be the last time you'll need it.

news.title: This Long-Lost Classic D&D RPG Is Finally Coming to Steam Soon
news.summary_raw: A 2001 follow-up to one of the most influential PC RPGs ever is returning after 25 years with 4K support, modern controls, an improved UI, Steam Deck compatibility, bug fixes, and an optional Legacy mode.

members.title: This Long-Lost Classic D&D RPG Is Finally Coming to Steam Soon

news.body:
This Long-Lost Classic D&D RPG Is Finally Coming to Steam Soon
A 2001 follow-up to one of the most influential PC RPGs ever is returning after 25 years with 4K support, modern controls, an improved UI, Steam Deck compatibility, bug fixes, and an optional Legacy mode.
In case you missed it
BioWare's Closure
Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor, a largely inaccessible Dungeons & Dragons RPG from the same era of BioWare’s original Baldur’s Gate games, is finally returning to PC. You can see the trailer on the Steam page.
Boutique publisher SNEG is working with Wizards of the Coast to restore the 2001 dungeon crawler for modern PCs. The new version launches for Steam and GOG on November 6, while a Steam Next Fest demo is currently available through October 26. Progress made in the demo will transfer to the full game.
Developed by Stormfront Studios and originally published by Ubisoft, Ruins of Myth Drannor arrived during an important period for D&D video games. BioWare had revitalized the computer RPG with Baldur’s Gate in 1998 and Baldur’s Gate II: Shadows of Amn in 2000, establishing a style built around memorable companions, expansive storytelling, player choice, and tactical real-time combat with pausing. Both of those followed the original Pool of Radiance games from the late 1980s and early 1990s. The original Pool of Radiance, released by Strategic Simulations in 1988, was the first officially licensed Advanced Dungeons & Dragons computer RPG.
Ruins of Myth Drannor approached the same tabletop license from a markedly different direction. Although it similarly presented its Forgotten Realms adventure from an isometric perspective, it emphasized dungeon exploration and turn-based tactical combat over BioWare’s dialogue-heavy, companion-driven narrative formula.
SNEG’s restoration will introduce widescreen resolutions up to 4K, upscaled backgrounds, full controller support, reworked camera controls, and an improved interface featuring a new action bar and additional tooltips. Players will also be able to adjust combat animation speeds, use Steam Cloud saves, unlock achievements, and play on Steam Deck.
An optional Legacy Mode will preserve the original presentation and gameplay for players seeking an experience closer to the 2001 release. SNEG also promises numerous bug fixes and quality-of-life improvements, which could be especially important for a game historically remembered as much for its technical problems as its ambition.
“Pool of Radiance: Ruins of Myth Drannor was an ambitious game for 2001. It has its own place in Dungeons & Dragons gaming history, but for years it has been challenging to experience on modern systems. Our goal with this re-release is simple: preserve what made the original special, fix what needs fixing, and make it accessible again to both longtime fans and a new generation of CRPG players.”
- Artem Shchuiko, SNEG Director
More than two decades later, Baldur’s Gate has become one of the defining names in modern RPGs, while Ruins of Myth Drannor largely disappeared from circulation. Its arrival on Steam and GOG offers players an opportunity to explore a different branch of D&D’s PC history, and to see how another ambitious studio translated tabletop adventuring during the genre’s turn-of-the-century resurgence.

news.body:
Podcast: Landfall's Rebecca Lautner on Peak's 23 million sales and looking past friendslop
Plus why Landfall works on games for just one month before deciding whether to drop them
A new episode of the still-somewhat-irregular GamesIndustry.biz podcast features a fireside chat with Rebecca Lautner, CBO at Landfall Games, recorded at Game Republic New Horizons. In conversation with features editor Lewis Packwood, Lautner says that even though Peak has now sold more than 23 million units, the developer is keen to move on to something else.
"From a business point of view, believe me, it's very frustrating sometimes because there's so much opportunity in there," she says. "But that's just not what we're about. And I learned to accept that really, really early on when I joined the team. I was like, okay, we have a very different path that we want to go, and it's fun."
Lautner also discusses the launch of publishing arm Evil Landfall, which backed this year's multi-million-selling smash hit How to Fish, but says the company is also looking to invest in a range of games beyond friendslop titles.
She also talks about Landfall's "fail fast" policy – where games are dropped after one month of development if they're not coming together – as well as Landfall's development house in Stockholm (which has its own chef and bar) and why there was no April Fools game this year.
You can find the episode right here, as well as on Spotify, YouTube and wherever you get your podcasts. Feedback is welcomed; you can reach me at jon.hicks@gamesindustry.biz.

news.body:
Marvel's Wolverine leads US September charts, achieves highest monthly dollar sales for a Sony-published title since Helldivers 2
PlayStation 5 spending rose 43% year over year, while unit sales increased 22%, according to Circana
Marvel's Wolverine led US game sales in September, achieving the highest monthly dollar sales for a Sony-published title since Helldivers 2.
Sony continued its hardware momentum, with PlayStation 5 leading both unit and dollar sales according to Circana data.
PS5 spending rose 43% year over year, and unit sales increased 22%, resulting in Sony's highest monthly hardware dollar share since May 2025.
Overall hardware spending rose 12% to $362 million in September, offsetting declines in dollar sales for Nintendo Switch 2 (down 12%) and Xbox Series X|S (down 2%).
Xbox Series X|S unit sales declined 27% in the US last month, with Xbox Ecosystem console sales reaching a record September low. Switch 2 unit sales decreased 14%.
Total content spending dropped 2% to $4.2 billion in September, led by a 14% decline in mobile. Console spending grew 8%, and PC spending rose 27%.
Eight new games debuted on the US chart in September. Marvel's Wolverine moved NBA 2K27 to No. 2 and outperformed EA Sports FC 27.
Despite its drop, NBA 2K27 surpassed Resident Evil Requiem to become the best-selling game of 2026 year-to-date.
Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave and Blood of the Dawnwalker completed the Top 5. Other new September entries included Wardogs, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, Halloween: The Game, and Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve.
Overall projected spending across content, hardware, and accessories declined 1% in September to $4.8 billion.

members.title: “我这就是个低俗游戏”｜机核专访《无比坚硬：荒原骑士》制作人

features.body:
在B站上，有款独立游戏凭借几部抽象，但又极具个性的预告片火了。光怪陆离的视效，离奇抽象的文字，似乎是一个发了癫的艺术家在舞台上一边大火煮着菌子，一边纵情表演。现代主义，解构，叽里咕噜，杀死月亮。
我不懂，于是我找到了《无比坚硬》的制作人，面对面发起了攻击。但是，我一拳打在了棉花上，因为制作人说要带我打台球——而我，答应了。
在采访期间，我也亲自坐到了开发者的位置上，直接通过游戏引擎，试玩到了《无比坚硬》。它就和宣传片里一样癫狂，抽象，让我没头没尾但一波又一波地感受到惊喜或者惊吓，使我露出了快乐的笑容。
目前正值Steam新品节，大家可以去steam上搜索《无比坚硬：荒原骑士》，下载DEMO试玩一下。也和我一样，亲自感受下仿佛从地上捡的一部“黑超梦”。
提问：作为游戏创作者，到底受到了什么样的影响，才会做出这样的一款游戏？
其实我觉得我其实一开始并没有想要做游戏这个方向。嗯，我是做着做着就变成这样子了。
其实本质原因就是我很讨厌做的跟别人很像，就我做所有东西的核心就是我讨厌做的别人很像，就是为了跟别人不像，成了我做游戏最大的快乐。如果做的跟别人很像，我会觉得无聊，我会变得很虚无。
就到公司里，可能就在坐那里喝杯奶茶，躺那里，好像人生就没意思，就会觉得没劲，也没有表达欲，就是「专业」这个事情是会让我觉得很沮丧。所以我做这个游戏，其实本质上我不是说一开始奔着这个东西来，我的本质是反抗，别人做的东西我就不想做，只是反抗。
之前干了一堆蠢事。做过游戏，拍过电影，然后搞过搞过摇滚乐，什么事都搞。去新疆拍过独立电影。
当时网剧很火的，短剧很火的时候，我就跑去新疆拍那个独立电影去了。也是拍那种现代主义的东西。后面又搞摇滚乐。反正一事无成（笑），干了很多蠢事，结果什么事没做出来。我又觉得要搞点什么，不然闲的没事。就属于那种，就老师提问，然后你举手，老师问你，你说我不知道。
当时在新疆那边搞了一辆坦克300，然后我坐副驾驶，听开车的大哥吹牛逼。我觉得那个挺爽，挺开心。拍独立电影，搞摇滚音乐也是，觉得酷。
提问：我在玩游戏的时候，明显感到里面有一些发癫的、抽象的气质在里面。这和您在武汉这个地方有关吗？
我虽然不是武汉人，但我在武汉呆了十多年了，武汉的神人确实非常多。
我经常晚上去东湖。我一个人在晚上三四点，跑去东湖。那时东湖完全没人。然后自己就会很开心，整个东湖是你的，然后我就在湖边溜达，很开心。
（东湖虽然是武汉5A级景区，但多是本地人散步郊游的好去处。景区面积十分巨大，超过80平方千米，因此哪怕是过年期间，也能寻找到一片安静宽敞的幽静之地。）
也不是，反正就是有时候 emo 了，然后找个地方消解一下。
其实游戏想法对我来说不是一个很大的限制，只要我愿意想，基本上都有很多点子。
我觉得难点是——现代主义有最大的问题就是就会很消极。我什么都不想动，那我该如何克服消极？这是个矛盾点，一个人一旦消极，他就不会做东西；但一个人很积极，他就不现代主义。这又是个悖论。
人声很嘈杂，就越来越没劲，你就没有动力，你没有热情做。但是游戏你又要有打起精神来，去公司里面工作干活，想点子，安排大家一起把东西弄出来。这就又需要积极性，所以这两个博弈点是我觉得是最大的痛苦。
提问：在做游戏的过程中，肯定会遇到各种各样的问题吧，能讲讲在游戏开发过程中遇到的困难吗？
我觉得有第一个最大的问题，就是很难让大家信任我，团队成员对我的信任。
就是说如果你去借鉴其他已有的东西，其实是很容易得到大家信任的。比如说我借鉴宫崎英高的魂，我做个类似的作品。你只是说你，我们能做到魂的60%，70%，大家都会觉得 ok！
（也就是说，想要把自己大脑里的那部分想法，正确无误地传达给团队，并让他们理解，是一件比较困难的事情对吗？）
对。其实我之前也也经历过这种事情，之前我会听大家的意见，也会积极地听玩家的意见，大家意见我都会听。但是这样就有个代价，你会变成一个项目经理，诶，而不是一个艺术家。成了海底捞的产品经理，顾客有什么不舒服，我就改。
这是一个逐步与团队建立信心的过程，反正我之前是跟有些同事是有些分歧的。对，他他会觉得“我看不懂你到底想做什么，你为什么要做这种？”
其实我拍电影之前，比较年轻的时候也做过游戏，虽然当时做的就不如我意，但也确实赚到了钱。
就是在那时候，我才发现一个核心——艺术是暴君，艺术是暴君（重复两遍！）。就是暴君，你必须笃定的完成你想要说的一切话，并且排除一切干扰你的信息。这个很难的。
很难排除，你知道为什么吗？你有没发现，现在所有的 UE 作品做的越来越像某个游戏吗？越来越像。对，就是因为他没有勇气去排除这个干扰项。
而且我们中国人有个常话叫三人行必有我师，就三个人聊天就有一个人是我的师傅，就这个东西从小接受的教育就三个人必有我师，是什么？三个人聊天一定有个人能让我学到东西。哇，你从小在这种环境中长大，你怎么可能排除这些干扰项？
工作以来，光是排除干扰项，就这一个过程花了我 10 年。
什么意思呢？我再也不会听任何人给我的意见了。我再也不会听任何人对我的反对了。我必须一意孤行地做出我内心的东西。
我可以接受我的项目失败，但我不能接受说我没有做到一意孤行。什么意思呢？
就是说，我也会被宫崎英高的作品征服，因为我基本把宫崎英高作品也全部通关了。但是，宫崎英高只能暂时征服我，而不能永久征服我。
提问：那么，随心所欲地，孤注一掷地，不受任何影响地做游戏会让你觉得特别开心，对吗？
也不会，因为因为人获得自由之后又会陷入第二个阶段，就是无聊。
因为自由的无聊就就有点像学校里面停电，然后你获得了一种自由，你就很开心。但等到你放暑假，或者天天放假，其实你也没有多开心。人类永远逃出不了人类本身的局限性，只是说会好玩一点，开心一点，也就只有一点。
提问：在开发的过程中有没有这种有趣的事可以分享？宣传片中的那首歌是你唱的吗？
跟大家团队沟通中也会有些事情很开心，就团队跟大家一起想，一起想个东西会很开心。你说的是我们一起唱的那首《友谊天长地久》是吧？其实当时就随便一录呗，就想唱歌。我突发奇想，就是那天突然决定的，临时起意。
你知道吗？采访的时候是一个人最无聊的时候。对。真的不骗你，所有人采访都很无聊。其实我我自己也观察过一些采访节目，就一个人被采访的时候就很无聊。
你知道一个人什么时候比较可爱吗？就是他平时最常规的状态。就是吹牛逼的时候。就是在项目中吹牛逼的时候，是不是比较可爱？你应该见过我平时吹牛逼的样子。
第一种情况就比如在项目吹牛逼的时候；第二是我打台球的时候。唉，那时候我就状态好。
就在台球厅里面跟那些台球助教吹牛逼的时候，她们都喜欢我。我自己也喜欢那个时候的我，就特别特别纯真。也不装逼，就天天跟那几个台球助教吹牛逼。
提问：在宣传片里有引用名著，比如你们引用了詹姆斯乔伊斯的《都柏林人》。对于您来说，在开发这部作品的时候，有哪些文学作品影响到了您？
我觉得影响最多的是卡夫卡，卡夫卡的作品。现代主义嘛，奠基人。还有就是陀思妥耶夫斯基。还有什么？还有个话剧吧，叫《等待戈多》也影响很多。电影的话，昆汀的作品对我影响比较多。
提问：话说，您年轻的时候也是拍文艺片的吧，肯定看了不少北欧的闷片。
对。我以前的时候为了装逼，你知道吗？看了好多北欧闷片。
我以前年轻的时候，在文艺青年里混嘛，这帮人很装逼的。就几个人聊天，“欸，有个片子你没看？”
我我认识一帮硬核的文艺青年，就一旦说个片子没看过，哎呀，“你都没有看过伯格曼的野草莓吗？”然后就嗤之以鼻。那时年轻的我为了融入他们，闷片，黑白片，各种看。
一天看五六部，就那北欧闷片，一部部看，硬着头看，但其实一点都不好看。
提问：那些片子就是对你现在开发游戏有影响吗？有帮助吗？
如果闷片是对的，那我应该是天天在家里看书的那帮人了，我为什么每天跑台球厅跟那些助教吹牛逼？年轻的时候，文艺电影，文学名著我天天看，我一个人能一天晚上看 5 遍黑白片。以前天天看这个东西，但没用啊，我都没有被拯救。这些东西都不能让我得到内心的自洽和平静，那对我来说，这些东西都是错的。
我更相信那些低俗的东西，我更相信粗鄙低俗的东西，因为这个就是真相。
我承认，哈哈哈哈哈。我这就是个低俗游戏。
提问：其实到最后就会游戏开发变得没那么浪漫，首先最重要的一点是——制作组的钱是怎么来的？
钱啊，在年轻时候做垃圾游戏挣了一点。做手游，做垃圾手游赚了一点。我拍电影的钱都是做垃圾手游赚的。也没有很多，就赚了一点。
以上就是与《无比坚硬》的制作人面对面采访的内容，与其说是解析游戏，不如说是对制作人的一次拷问。想必大家也能感受到，为什么《无比坚硬》会以这样一个方式呈现在玩家面前。
游戏目前在战斗上呈现的模样还较为早期，虽然架子搭好了，但还有大量的细节需要打磨，期待早日推出正式版~
等到游戏正式售卖的时候，制作人要带我去打台球，届时我也会及时与大家通告最新消息！

features.body:
# #2 游戏的高度严肃性

玩是谦恭，不是解放

本文在腾云公众号发布时，名字为《游戏的态度：如果不“严肃”，你就无法感受它的魅力》



### 引子

*有一种错觉是，游戏之所以吸引人，是因为你可以在游戏世界里“为所欲为”。但事实恰恰相反，游戏的迷人之处，正是因为它的规则性，或者说“限制性”。*

*另一个错觉是，因为游戏太“真实”，所以人们才心甘情愿“陷”在其中。事实上，和看电影类似，人们是主动选择将自己置身于一种“假信”的状态，并以此感受其中的乐趣。*

*这些“错觉”的存在，恰恰说明了“游戏”和“严肃”如影随形。*

*而“严肃”或许是最好的“游戏态度”。*

### 00 孩子教给大人的事

> “我想要把这本书献给我六岁的儿子山姆......**他教会了我以严肃的态度看待并体验游戏，让我自始至终都乐在其中。”**【1】

在《游戏改变学习：游戏素养、批判性思维与未来教育》一书的序言中，美国著名语言学学者詹姆斯·保罗·吉这样感谢他六岁的儿子。

以严肃的态度来看待游戏，许多人都可以理解，但是“以严肃的态度来体验游戏”，这是什么意思？

在游戏中，严肃与玩乐相伴而行，形成一种辨证的诡辞（dialectic paradox），在限制与自由、谦恭与解放之间，“严肃”就像是一个捉摸不透却总是处处闪现的“幽灵”，总想摆脱人们对它的思考和定义。

让我们从游戏的“严肃性”谈起。

### 01 **没有严肃性就没有游戏**

> 没有比游戏更严肃的事【2】。—— 法国哲学家亨利·列斐伏尔

这种说法乍听起来有些不可思议。但我甚至要说：“严肃性”才是游戏成立的基础。这里的“严肃”指的是一种游戏者的心态，一种“假装”(make-believe)。

举例来说，当我们与孩子玩耍时，会假装看不见蹩脚地躲在窗帘背后的孩子；我们在踢球的时候，会假装与对方是对抗的敌人；动物们在追逐嬉戏的时候，即便不会伤害对方，也会装作在捕猎而轻咬打闹。

荷兰文化史学家赫伊津哈在《游戏的人》中也举了一个让人印象深刻的例子：“一位父亲发现四岁的儿子坐在一排椅子的前端玩‘开火车’游戏。他拥抱儿子的时候，男孩说：‘别亲火车头，爸爸，不然车厢就知道它不是真的了。’ ”【3】

**每个孩子都心知肚明他“只是在假装（only-pretending）”，但这种“假装”绝不是一种不严肃的态度。这种假装实际上是一种对于规则的认可，对于游戏某种虚构本质视而不见却又沉浸其中的态度的“严肃”，才能让这个游戏进行下去。**



人类学家罗杰凯瓦卢（Roger Caillois）将其称之为假装Make-Believe，一种与现实相对应的非现实性/第二现实的特殊态度。【4】

哲学家伯纳尔·舒兹在《蚱蜢：游戏，生命与乌托邦》中则将其称之为“游戏态度（Lusory attitude，拉丁文ludus，意指游戏）”，指这样一种“奇异”的状态：人们接受游戏规则限制采取效率低下的方法，而非用直接且高效的方式来达成目标。【5】

**这种假装与严肃的态度还体现在对游戏规则的遵守。**

游戏都有前游戏目标（Pre-lusory Goal），例如四百米赛跑，目标就是从起点跑到终点；同时有我们要遵守的规则（Constitutive Rules），我们并不能骑着自行车去拿长跑第一名，或者是开着作弊器违反规则通关游戏之后说——我赢了！因为你在违反规则，或者说参与游戏的这种"假装"的时候，你已经离开了游戏。



**因此，游戏绝不仅仅是嬉皮笑脸、毫无规矩。事实恰恰相反。**

荷兰语言学家赫伊津哈一直把“扫兴的人”作为理解游戏意义的关键。所谓“扫兴的人”，就是那些触犯规则、无视规则的人，这样的搅局者（spoil-sport）褫夺了游戏的幻觉，也是游戏者最反感的。

举例来说，在餐桌上行酒令，输了游戏却不愿接受惩罚的人一定会被人“看扁”；下棋的时候，我们也不愿意和那些违反“落棋无悔”规则的人下棋；看直播的时候，我们对于开挂者和作弊者的愤怒，对于假赛和不全力以赴之人的鄙视......都说明游戏里的“搅局者”是不受欢迎的。

**由此我们也可以发现，游戏的意义与魅力并不在于人们通常认为的“自由”或是“解放”，而恰恰是在于游戏本身的“限制条件”，在于游戏使人必须“遵守规则”。**

这是“游戏”与“玩”的悖论：“乐趣源于对自由的限制而不是对自由的放纵。【6】”

### 02 **假信：游戏和艺术的“异曲同工”**

可别小瞧这种“严肃性”与“假装”。这样的态度不仅仅存在于孩子们搭沙堡、过家家游戏中，同样和审美/艺术相关联。

“小男孩将一根木棍当作木马，假装在骑马以获取乐趣。”在《木马沉思录》中，艺术史家贡布里希著名以这种“假信”为起点，探究所有艺术形式的根源。

这种“假信”的态度可以在很多艺术形式的审美中找到。

例如，对于文学作品的欣赏，有一种被称之为“怀疑搁置(suspension of disbelief)”的状态。这一概念由诗人塞缪尔·泰勒·柯尔律治所创造，指的是读者主动接受故事荒谬或在现实世界中“不可能”的地方【7】，并享受其中。如何理解？

**你可以想象一下，如果你在阅读奇幻小说时忍不住去质疑“世界上哪有这么大的龙？”“怎么可能有人脱水了还能活着？”等这些场景的“荒谬”，那么你可能会与《权力的游戏》或《三体》等作品中最震撼人心的场景失之交臂。因为你不愿意让自己处于“假信”的状态。**

同理，演员的专业表演、固定的座椅、安静的空间...电影院或剧院的这些规则，都是为了让观众忘记现实，沉浸在导演营造的叙事中。

这种在电影院中仿佛置身另一个世界而假装忘记现实的体验是十分重要的。这也是为什么大卫林奇认为，倘若在手机上播放电影，那么“一万年也无法体验电影”。【8】

一旦这种“假信”的状态被“揭穿”，在场的所有人就会从陶醉的美梦中惊醒——打破了尼采所说的观众的施魔(Verzauberung)。美妙的体验便瞬间消失。



> 玩是谦恭，不是解放。——伊恩·博格斯特（Ian Bogost）

**更进一步说，游戏规则之下的“严肃性”和“假装”中蕴含着一种对于事物的“尊重感”。**

玩家心甘情愿接受这些规则，进入这个游戏所创造的魔圈（magic circle）之中；观众同样仿佛都约定好了似的，进入电影和戏剧“不真实”的世界里。在这种状态中，人不再是以自己为中心，而是去接受事物本身的设置，去倾听艺术的声音，去接受艺术作品。

也就是说，人们心甘情愿地放下自我为中心的主体地位，而与处于客体的事物共同游戏。

在电影院里，与被“固定”在座椅上、不能随意移动、不能大声说话的观影者相比，电影本身反而成为了一个“行动者”，它仿佛在用自身的光影刺向身处黑暗中的观众，让他们被触动（affected）。【9】

**也就是说，自认为最具有能动性（agency）的人类，在电影院中恰恰不是特别“有生气”（vibrant）。如果从“非人类中心主义”的视角来看，事实确实如此。**



电子游戏也是如此。

玩家需要主动放弃自己身体的运动，放弃多余的感知方式，去接受一个由游戏设计师设定好的、由交互与反馈构成的“角色替身”（avatar）。当然，还有那些游戏世界中的复杂规则。

在这样的限制中，当玩家的操作变得越来越娴熟，他就能够感受到动作游戏中操作的美感，感受到游戏中的角色就像玩家感官和身体的延伸。一种虚拟的运动感（kinesthesia）与本体感受（proprioception）【10】被构建出来。

表面上，游戏角色是被玩家所操控的，但实际上，玩家也受着游戏和角色的限制——游戏角色或游戏成为一种具有自己生命力的主体，一种“拟生命”(quasi-life)，反过来限制和操控着玩家。【11】

**玩家在这样对限制的接受和发挥、被动与主动、操控与反操控之间，感受到游戏的美感与乐趣。**

从这个角度出发，或许就可以理解为什么哲学家伽达默尔将 “游戏作为艺术作品的存在方式”。因为游戏/艺术不再是一个对象化的客体，而成为卷入游戏者的主体，被动而却又含有主动性的意义(der mediale sinn)。

这也是为什么说游戏和艺术有异曲同工之处。

因为游戏和所有艺术的运作方式，都涉及到观众/玩家的一种“参与限制”又“超越限制”的审美状态。事实上，只有这样才能感受到美的存在。当然，这里也涉及到现代人应该具备的一种能力：一种能够沉浸在事物之中，遵守规则而体会事物的规律与美好之处的能力。

### 03 **辩证的游戏态度：“无用”游戏的魔法**

> “或许一个人如果想体会到生活中的浪漫情调就必须在某种程度上是一个演员；而要想跳出自身之外，则必须能够对自己的行动抱着一种既超然物外又沉浸于其中的兴趣。” —— 毛姆

前文说游戏的成立核心在于严肃的遵守规则、接受限制而追逐目标、沉浸在游戏之中。但当游戏结束，我们其实都明白：它只是一场游戏，It's just for fun（这只是为了开心），it's not real（这并不是真的）。

**玩游戏的人知道自己在玩游戏。**玩游戏的人知道它的结果其实并不重要，它是“无意义”的，Roger Caillois将其定义为非生产性的（Unproductive）。

简单来说：游戏本质上是“无用”的。

游戏要达成的目标是没有意义且微不足道的（例如把高尔夫球放进洞里，或者是电子游戏这样的干脆虚构出来的目标）。

有些人对于大部分游戏不感兴趣，或者说，提不起兴趣，很大的原因就来自于这里，他们用功利主义或目标论的标准来看游戏，游戏就是完全无意义的。

但奇特的辩证法就在于此，参与游戏中的人们并不是因为游戏的目标十分重要，或者游戏可以给自己带来什么样的好处去玩游戏，而仅仅因为游戏的过程中的体验。他们愿意进行严肃的参与，愿意去做这样的一件在寻常价值体系下毫无价值的事情。而这往往就是乐趣和意义的魔法发生的地方。

**这里所提倡的是一种辨证的游戏态度，超然物外而又沉浸其中。**

相反的，当很多人误把游戏的目标当做游戏的价值，为了得到某些游戏内的数值，达到某个段位，为了游戏的目标（实际上是微不足道的）而废寝忘食，醒悟过来后发现这些目标对现实没有任何价值（当然了，这就是游戏的特点）。

如果当我们只是一心为了游戏中虚构的目标而努力，忽略了过程。亦或在过程中没有感到丝毫乐趣却依旧在重复性地游玩，那我们并不在游戏，而在工作与劳作。



###

### 04 **缺乏游戏态度的现代人**

当你因游戏而忘了吃饭时间，你的母亲或许会感到不理解，而你也很难向她作出解释。

这是因为，你们之间存在一个错位：

母亲所看到的是游戏这项活动的非必要性/非生产性的一面——即“游戏只不过是游戏”；而此时，她的孩子正全心全意正扑在游戏中——他暂时忘记了“现实”，他正灵活运用这游戏世界中的符号，符号背后是他与九个真实的人在先前的三十分钟里的投入，所以**他对此十分严肃——而这也正是游戏得以成立与展开的基础，也是这个孩子能够进行游戏，并享受游戏乐趣的基本条件与要求**。

这或许是现在的整个社会上对电子游戏存在的错位。

游戏玩家的游戏态度让其投入其中，但有些人过了头沉迷游戏，而那些站在电子游戏外部的人困惑并对这种社会现象指指点点，他们并不能投入其中，也并没有玩游戏的能力。

想要学会玩游戏并不是那么简单的。

这里首先需要一种游戏素养（Game literacy），也就是接受一套新的规则，一套新的符号系统并且灵活运用的能力。

就像《游戏设计之快乐理论》或者是许多游戏设计者和思考者将游戏看作是对于某种模式（pattern）的学习一样，《游戏改变学习》一书中将游戏的过程其称之为批判式的学习。前提在于，首先我们要主动，且自愿地面对游戏提供给的一种新的学习以及思维方式，要自愿地去接受一套规则。【12】

好比一个从来没有接触过《英雄联盟》的玩家，它需要学习游戏中的上百个英雄，记住其对应的技能形象，出装，并且能够在学习中逐渐把握到整体游戏战场节奏的变化，用书中的话来说：“学会用新视角来定位词语/图像/标识/物品等事物的意义，建立新联系。”

还有一种最重要的态度，也就是这篇文章谈论的：

在生活和工作节奏如此快速的今天，我们能够保有一种不“功利”的态度，在认识到游戏“目标无用”的前提下，花时间去严肃和真诚地做“无用之事”，这本身就是珍贵的。这需要一种对事物本身的好奇，对创造物与艺术品的尊重和投入，更需要不凡的创造力。

**“世间最肤浅的莫过于以浅薄的姿态面对正经事，世间最引人入胜的莫过于对待琐事的事后显示出你之所为绝非琐事。”** 伊拉斯谟在他的传世名篇《愚人颂》的开头这样写道。

或许玩亦是自制、亦是自由，如同玩家可主动接受游戏的规则限制与他人共享乐趣，亦可跳脱出来进行批判性思考，将游戏看做一个系统、一个被设计的空间，进行再创造和超越，并评判游戏的好坏。那就有待下篇文章去扩展了【13】

features.title: Keys to Combat Design: Anatomy of an Attack
features.title_cn: 战斗设计要点：拆解一次攻击的构成
features.editor_note: 来自现有收藏；讨论攻击动作的分段与战斗设计。
features.body:
Welcome to the next article on a series dedicated to Combat Design! It all started with one article, but it quickly became apparent that this topic is way too wide and complex to be able to tackle it with a single one.
This series is the logical succession of the article Keys to Rational Enemy Design, so make sure you check it out.
In this series, we will talk about all the components that a designer needs to consider to produce a snappy, meaningful, rewarding, skill-based fight:
- Pacing
- Enemy AI and decision trees
- Group AI
- Player’s abilities and metrics
- Player’s strategies
- Difficulty management and rationalization
- Hitboxes and Hurtboxes
- …
- And, of course, attacks, our topic of the day.
We are starting this series with this topic because attacks are the most core component of a fight. Dissecting what makes up an attack, both for the player and for the enemies the player is fighting will put in light the keys to a good fight: readability, fairness, skill, challenge, purpose…
We will talk about the different phases of an attack, about Windows of Opportunity (or WoO in short), about animation, about input lag… And, hopefully, you will have at the end of this article all the keys to challenge your own fight system and recognize the elements that make games like Hollow Knight or Nioh so good in that domain.
But before we start, it’s important to understand the scope of what we will discuss: by combat, we mean any real-time armed confrontation between the player and one or more enemies. Our study will then be independent of said weapons, being fists, melee weapons, or ranged weapons. Street Fighter, Punch-Out, For Honor, Assassin’s Creed, Hollow Knight, Cuphead, Mordhau, Dark Soul… Every one of these games confronts the player using globally the same design rules, and these are the ones we will break down today, starting with the enemy’s side of it.
Enemy’s Attacks
In order to properly design an attack, we first need to understand what phases compose an attack. An enemy attack is on paper very straightforward, and always made of three distinct elements:
Think of it as in real life: should you want to throw a kick, you will first start preparing your body for it, bending your body backward, and arming your leg. This is the anticipation. Then comes the attack, the very small part that is about hitting the opponent. Finally, once the attack finishes, your body will have to go to its final resting position (that could be the original one): this is the recovery.
Well, attacks in video games work in the exact same way:
One reason is of course because our players, though playing in a fictional world, expect real-life constraints and forces to apply in it too: gravity, weight, anatomy, physiology… But we will come to that when talking about animation.
Another reason, and one that is particularly interesting for us game designers, is that these three phases are critical for the gameplay, each one of them in its own way. They are the base for players’ tactics to emerge and are carefully crafted to balance difficulty, challenge abilities, and drive playstyles.
Let’s develop each of them using the player experience as the common thread of this article.
Key #1: Every single attack should be broken down into 3 phases: Anticipation, Attack, and Recovery.
Anticipation
The anticipation of an attack is, in essence, a Sign for the player that a specific attack is coming (see. Keys to Signs & Feedback). It’s a warning. It will drive the player to get away before the attack happens, block, dodge, or even push his luck and try hitting the enemy to interrupt the attack.
For the anticipation phase to fill its role properly, it must comply with a few rules:
- The animation of each anticipation must be unique: no other attack from this enemy can have the same anticipation (except if you want to pull a twist on your players, who am I to judge). And by unique, I mean drastically different. Subtleties are lost in the heat of a fight, players won’t ever see that an enemy slightly changed its stance before starting a different attack, and it will ultimately lead to frustration.
- The animation of each anticipation must hint at its follow-up attack: a player shouldn’t have to rely on memorization and trial and error to learn how to defeat an enemy. The animation, just like in real life, should follow logic (for example, bringing an ax behind your body before splitting a log in two). Record and study your players’ first encounter with your enemies. Even if they get hit by an attack, they should have seen it coming and started reacting accordingly.
Key #2: an efficient Anticipation translates in a unique warning animation, telegraphing the incoming attack.
Cuphead is a beautiful reference to study. Their over-exaggerated animation style and the cartoon codes of the 1930s allowed them to really create the most legible combat animations I’ve seen in a game.
I mean… Look at that anticipation!
Now that we talked about animation unicity and continuity there is still one big point to discuss relative to the anticipation: timing. How long should this anticipation last? Or, in development terms: how many frames must the anticipation have? Well, unfortunately, there is no clear rule for that as it depends on two factors: what action do you expect the player to do (and how long does it take to do it)? And what is the extra margin you want to give them? Remember that acknowledging an incoming danger and reacting to it isn’t immediate for a human being (unfortunately).
As a rule of thumb, consider that the reaction time of a player will be 0.25 seconds (so around 8 frames in a 30fps game, and 15 frames in a 60fps one). Now let’s say you want the player to block a specific attack, and that the block will be efficient at the end of its animation, 10 frames after the press of the block button by the player. The minimum anticipation time will be 10+8= 18 frames! Of course, other variables could affect this number: the extra frames the weapon will need to reach the players based on their distance from the enemy, the input lag, etc. But you get the idea.
The difficulty of dodging/parrying/interrupting/blocking the attack will then crystallize in a single metric: how much of an extra buffer do you give your players on top of this minimum anticipation time? This part will be a constant fine-tuning between players and developers. Playtests are key.
Key #3: Anticipation time = (player’s reaction time) + (expected player’s ability trigger time) + (difficulty buffer).
Attack
The attack part is the most obvious for us to imagine as it mimics perfectly real-life scenarios. The enemy will try to use its weapon (a fist, a sword, a gun) to hit a vulnerable part of our player: usually its body. Easy enough.
That being said, there are a lot of subtleties that will make an attack feel good. What we are looking for here is a sharp, snappy feeling and not a sloppy unpredictable one.
When designing an attack, you want it to be:
- Instant
- Unambiguous
- With a clear intent
- Precise
- Driving a specific player’s reaction
It seems straight-forward enough and yet plenty of games miss the spot with these directions. Having an instant attack means that your animation must not be longer than a few frames from the end of the anticipation to the start of the recovery. This means you will probably have to bend the laws of physics slightly to exaggerate the movement. Of course, we can find plenty of examples of extremely slow, pressuring attacks but these do not change the goal we are trying to achieve: we want the player to be able to tell exactly when the attack will land. Any blurriness at that moment will result in a sloppy, frustrating attack.
Driving a specific player’s reaction and being unambiguous means that you want your attack to be pretty stereotypical and its metrics to fit the player’s abilities. For example, you do not want a wavy, diagonal attack with varying speed. Instead, you will prefer a clean horizontal swipe with a constant speed.
Look at that Yokai’s double attack from Nioh:
Remember what I was saying about bending the laws of physics? The anticipation is slow and involves the entire Yokai’s body, showcasing the insane weight (and deadly power) of that ax. Considering the struggle to lift this weapon, there is no way the demon could swing it that fast. But at that specific moment, anatomy and realism do not matter. What matters is that his swing is instant and perfectly horizontal, allowing the player to precisely time his dodge under it.
The follow-up attack follows the same principles: perfectly vertical and happening in a blink. You will notice that this attack cannot hit a player that dodged the first hit (the Yokai doesn’t reorient mid-attack). It is used either as a Window of Opportunity (WoO) for the players to land their own counter-attack or a double punishment should a player get hit by the first blow.
Key #4: an attack is instant, constant, and with a very small amount of varying parameters.
Side note: look at the anticipation. It is unique, recognizable, and without subtleties. The downside I see is how close this ax rotation is from looking like an attack. Nioh actually deals with these issues (as they are common among their enemies) by adding a VFX to the weapon during the attack phase (i.e. the dangerous part). Weapon trails are very efficient Signs and support the learning and understanding of the attacks and patterns of enemies. Plenty of games use this trick, you could consider it too!
Key #5: Adding a weapon trail VFX to all attacks, following the weapon and its hitbox, is a clean way to highlight its deadly part (and the VFX persistence will underline the attack direction).
Recovery
Finally, once an attack has been performed, comes the recovery. And let’s make it clear right away, the goal of this phase is extremely simple: give the player a clear Window of Opportunity. A window to hit back, to heal, to run away, to reload, to plan

I added four player online mode to Battledrones - previous maps were limited to two.
Here's the initial prompt I used:
Add a new map for a four player battle - four way rotational symmetry, up to four AI players, works with the WebSocket non-audio based multiplayer mode so up to four human players can join (any spare slots use AI)
Claude Opus 5.5 added a new map called "Compass Rose" and modified the WebSockets multiplayer network code to support up to four players for that map, joining via share links or QR codes.
The new teams use robots themed in purple and green, joining the existing blue and red designs. You can preview those colors in the updated model browser.
